Overview

To improve performance and reduce storage overhead, databases can use external storage for certain columns. This type of storage is used for columns that store large amounts of data, such as the PostgreSQL TOAST (The Oversized-Attribute Storage Technique), Oracle Large Object (LOB), or the Oracle Exadata Extended String data types. To reduce I/O overhead and increase query speed, when data changes in a table row, the database retrieves only the columns that contain new values, ignoring data in externally stored columns that remain unchanged. As a result, the value of the externally stored column is not recorded in the database log, and Debezium subsequently omits the column when it emits the event record. Downstream consumers that receive event records that omit required values can experience processing errors.

If a value for an externally stored column is not present in the database log entry for an event, when Debezium emits a record for the event, it replaces the missing value with an unavailable.value.placeholder sentinel value. These sentinel values are inserted into appropriately typed fields, for example, a byte array for bytes, a string for strings, or a key-value map for maps.

To retrieve data for columns that were not available in the initial query, you can apply the Debezium reselect columns post processor (ReselectColumnsPostProcessor). You can configure the post processor to reselect one or more columns from a table. After you configure the post processor, it monitors events that the connector emits for the column names that you designate for reselection. When it detects an event with the specified columns, the post processor re-queries the source tables to retrieve data for the specified columns, and fetches their current state.

You can configure the post processor to reselect the following column types:

  • null columns.

  • Columns that contain the unavailable.value.placeholder sentinel value.

Note
 You can use the ReselectColumnsPostProcessor post processor only with Debezium source connectors. The post processor is not designed to work with the Debezium JDBC sink connector.

Keyless tables

The reselect columns post processor generates a reselect query that returns the row to be modified. To construct the WHERE clause for the query, by default, the post processor uses a relational table model that is based on the table’s primary key columns or on the unique index that is defined for the table.

For keyless tables, the SELECT query that ReselectColumnsPostProcessor submits might return multiple rows, in which case Debezium always uses only the first row. You cannot prioritize the order of the returned rows. To enable the post processor to return a consistently usable result for a keyless table, it’s best to designate a custom key that can identify a unique row. The custom key must be capable of uniquely identify records in the source table based on a combination of columns.

To define such a custom message key, use the message.key.columns property in the connector configuration. After you define a custom key, set the reselect.use.event.key configuration property to true. Setting this option enables the post processor to use the specified event key fields as selection criteria in lieu of a primary key column. Be sure to test the configuration to ensure that the reselection query provides the expected results.

Value caching

By default, the post processor queries the database for every event that requires reselection. For workloads in which the same rows are reselected repeatedly (for example, TOAST or LOB columns that Debezium emits as placeholders on every unrelated row update), you can enable an optional cache of reselected values to reduce the number of database queries.

Enable caching by setting reselect.cache.enabled to true. Reselected values are cached per row and per column, using the event’s message key as the cache key. Before querying the database, the post processor checks the cache for each column that requires reselection, and only queries columns that are not already cached. Eligible columns whose values are present in the event record are also written to the cache, even if no reselection is needed, so a later event that omits the same column can be served from the cache without querying the database again.

The cache is refreshed on modification: any event that carries a real (non-placeholder) value for an eligible column updates that column’s cache entry with the current value. As a result, a later event that does not modify the column can be served from the cache, and a cached value is never served after the column has changed.

Because the row identity is the message key, including its schema, a change to the key’s schema (for example, a DDL change or a primary-key reordering) yields a different cache key, so the post processor queries the database for the new key rather than returning a stale cached value.

The cache storage is pluggable through the reselect.cache.type property, which names an implementation of the io.debezium.processors.reselect.cache.ReselectColumnCache contract. Debezium provides the implementations described in the following sections; you can also supply a custom implementation to integrate an alternative backend. Custom implementations that store values outside the JVM heap can extend io.debezium.processors.reselect.cache.AbstractSerializingReselectColumnCache, which handles the conversion of row keys and column values to and from bytes and requires only simple byte-level get, put, and remove storage operations.

In-memory cache

The default cache implementation, io.debezium.processors.reselect.cache.MemoryReselectColumnCache, stores values on the JVM heap. The cache is bounded in both dimensions, the number of rows and the number of columns cached per row, and evicts the least-recently-used entries when a bound is exceeded. Cached values also expire after a time-to-live, which bounds how long entries for rows that are no longer being updated are retained in memory. The cache is lost when the connector stops, so reselections begin repopulating it after a restart.

The in-memory cache supports the following properties, in addition to the common reselect.cache.* properties:

Table 1. In-memory cache configuration options

Property

Default

Description

post.processors.reselect.cache.max.size

10000

The maximum number of cached rows retained in the reselection cache.

When the limit is reached, the least-recently-used entries are evicted.

post.processors.reselect.cache.ttl.ms

600000

The time-to-live, in milliseconds, of a cached reselection value.

Because the cache is refreshed on modification, this value only bounds how long entries for rows that are no longer being updated are retained in memory; it is not the mechanism that guarantees freshness.

post.processors.reselect.cache.max.columns.per.row

200

The maximum number of columns cached per row in the reselection cache.

When the limit is reached, the least-recently-used column entries for that row are evicted. This bound guards against wide tables (for example, tables with 500-1000 columns) growing the per-row inner map without limit.

RocksDB cache

The io.debezium.storage.rocksdb.reselect.RocksDbReselectColumnCache implementation persists cached values to disk in an embedded RocksDB database. Cached values persist after you a connector restarts, so columns that would otherwise need to be reselected continue to be served from the cache after a restart. Entries remain correct across restarts because the post processor refreshes the cache whenever a column arrives with a real value.

To use the RocksDB cache, the debezium-storage-rocksdb artifact must be on the connector plugin path, and reselect.cache.type must be set to the implementation’s fully-qualified class name.

Storage is permanent by default: no time-to-live is applied, and the database directory is retained when the connector stops. If you specify a positive reselect.cache.ttl.ms value, expired entries are treated as cache misses and removed when they are read. RocksDB reclaims expired entries from disk during compaction. A time-to-live is recommended for schemas that change frequently, because entries written under a previous key schema are never overwritten and would otherwise remain on disk indefinitely.

Note

The time-to-live setting determines how the RocksDB database is opened, and the two modes store entries on disk in different formats. If you change reselect.cache.ttl.ms between 0 and a positive value across a connector restart, entries that were written before the change can become unreadable in the new mode. Unreadable entries are discarded and treated as cache misses, so the affected columns are transparently reselected from the database and re-cached; no manual cleanup of the storage directory is required.
Important

RocksDB takes an exclusive lock on its storage directory. Configure a distinct reselect.cache.rocksdb.path for each connector, and for each task of a multi-task connector.

The following example shows a post-processor configuration that uses the RocksDB cache:

  "post.processors.reselector.reselect.cache.enabled" : "true",
  "post.processors.reselector.reselect.cache.type" : "io.debezium.storage.rocksdb.reselect.RocksDbReselectColumnCache",
  "post.processors.reselector.reselect.cache.rocksdb.path" : "/var/lib/debezium/reselect-cache"

The RocksDB cache supports the following properties, in addition to the common reselect.cache.* properties:

Table 2. RocksDB cache configuration options

Property

Default

Description

post.processors.reselect.cache.rocksdb.path

No default

The directory path in which the RocksDB database is stored. The directory is created if it does not exist. This property is required.

post.processors.reselect.cache.rocksdb.cleanup

false

Specifies whether the RocksDB database directory is deleted when the connector stops.

By default the directory is retained, so cached values persist across connector restarts.

post.processors.reselect.cache.ttl.ms

0

The time-to-live, in milliseconds, of a cached reselection value; 0 disables expiration so entries persist until overwritten or invalidated.

Note that this is the same property that the in-memory cache uses, but with a different default: persistent storage is permanent unless a time-to-live is explicitly configured.

Configuration example

Configuring a post processor is similar to configuring a custom converter or single message transformation (SMT). To enable the connector to use the ReselectColumnsPostProcessor, add the following entries to the connector configuration:

  "post.processors" : "reselector",
  "post.processors.reselector.type" : "io.debezium.processors.reselect.ReselectColumnsPostProcessor",
  "post.processors.reselector.reselect.columns.include.list" : "<schema>.<table>:<column>,<schema>.<table>:<column>",
  "post.processors.reselector.reselect.unavailable.values" : "true",
  "post.processors.reselector.reselect.null.values" : "true",
  "post.processors.reselector.reselect.use.event.key" : "false",
  "post.processors.reselector.reselect.error.handling.mode" : "WARN"

See the configuration options for the full list of available configuration properties.

Configuration options

The following table lists the configuration options that you can set for the Reselect Columns post-processor.

Table 3. Reselect columns post processor configuration options

Property

Default

Description

post.processors.reselect.columns.post.processors

No default

Comma-separated list of post processors to enable. Post processors run in the order that you list them.

`post.processors.reselector.type

No default

The fully-qualified class type name for the specified post processor.

post.processors.reselect.columns.include.list

No default

Comma-separated list of column names to reselect from the source database. If the values for the specified columns are not present in the change event, the post processor requeries the source table to retrieve the values. Use the following format to specify column names:

<schema>.<table>:<column>

Do not set this property if you set the post.processors.reselect.columns.exclude.list property.

post.processors.reselect.columns.exclude.list

No default

Comma-separated list of column names in the source database to exclude from reselection. Use the following format to specify column names:

<schema>.<table>:<column>

Do not set this property if you set the post.processors.reselect.columns.include.list property.

post.processors.reselect.unavailable.values

true

Specifies whether the post processor reselects a column that matches the post.processors.reselect.columns.include.list filter if the column value is provided by the connector’s unavailable.value.placeholder property.

post.processors.reselect.null.values

true

Specifies whether the post processor reselects a column that matches the post.processors.reselect.columns.include.list filter if the column value is null.

post.processors.reselect.use.event.key

false

Specifies whether the post processor reselects based on the event’s key field names or uses the relational table’s primary key column names.

By default, the reselection query is based on the relational table’s primary key columns or unique key index. For tables that do not have a primary key, set this property to true, and configure the message.key.columns property in the connector configuration to specify a custom key for the connector to use when it creates events. The post processor then uses the specified key field names as the primary key in the SQL reselection query.

post.processors.reselect.error.handling.mode

WARN

Specifies how the reselect post processor reacts to certain conditions.

By default, the post-processor logs a warning message when the row cannot be found or if there is a database selection error.

When set to FAIL, the connector will stop processing changes if the row no longer exists at the time of reselection or if there is a database failure when reselecting the row.

post.processors.reselect.cache.enabled

false

Enables an optional, per-column cache of reselected values.

By default the post processor queries the database for every event that requires reselection. When set to true, reselected column values are cached per row and column, and subsequent events that require the same column are served from the cache instead of querying the database. This is most useful for large, rarely-changing columns (such as TOAST or LOB values) on frequently-updated rows. See Value caching for a description of the caching mechanism.

post.processors.reselect.cache.type

io.debezium.processors.reselect.cache.MemoryReselectColumnCache

The fully-qualified name of the io.debezium.processors.reselect.cache.ReselectColumnCache implementation used to store reselected values. Applies only when reselect.cache.enabled is true.

Debezium provides the in-memory cache (the default) and the RocksDB cache (io.debezium.storage.rocksdb.reselect.RocksDbReselectColumnCache); each caches supports additional reselect.cache.* properties, as described in RocksDB cache.
